title: 2021 AMC 12A Problem 18
statement: Let \(f\) be a function defined on the set of positive rational numbers with the property that \(f(a\cdot b) = f(a) + f(b)\) for all positive rational numbers \(a\) and \(b.\) Suppose that \(f\) also has the property that \(f(p) = p\) for every prime number \(p.\) For which of the following numbers \(x\) is \(f(x) \lt 0?\)

solutions.text:
The functional equation makes \(f\) completely additive: for \(x = \prod p^{e_p},\) we have \(f(x) = \sum e_p\, f(p) = \sum e_p\, p,\) where a prime in the denominator contributes a negative exponent (since \(f(\frac{1}{p}) = -p\)).

Evaluating: \(f\!\left(\tfrac{17}{32}\right) = 17 - 5\cdot 2 = 7,\) \(f\!\left(\tfrac{11}{16}\right) = 11 - 4\cdot 2 = 3,\) \(f\!\left(\tfrac{7}{9}\right) = 7 - 2\cdot 3 = 1,\) \(f\!\left(\tfrac{7}{6}\right) = 7 - 2 - 3 = 2,\) and \(f\!\left(\tfrac{25}{11}\right) = 2\cdot 5 - 11 = -1.\) Only the last is negative.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: The rule makes \(f\) additive over prime factors, and \(f(\frac{1}{p}) = -f(p) = -p\)
For \(x = \prod p^{e_p},\) compute \(f(x) = \sum e_p\, p\) (with negative exponents for denominators)
